notes: MODULE STATE (2026-11-05): the TU defines its .data 0x0208e420..0x0208e498 (eleven objects) and .bss 0x0209b470..0x0209ba84 (seventeen objects plus the registry). An earlier note here called the module state all .bss and listed data_0209f250/2f8/394; that was wrong. 0x0208e420.. is initialized .data (four s8, three of them -1 and one 0x7f; six int words, all -1; then sPlayerSeqLimits), and 0x0209f250, gCurrentSublevel (0x0209f2f8) and 0x0209f394 are the stage TU's .bss (the 0x0209f1e8..0x0209f5b8 run, d_s_stage_methods.cpp), read here only.

Boundaries. .data starts where _ZTV8dActor_c ends (address point 0x0208e3a4, 0x84 bytes from 0x0208e39c, so it ends at 0x0208e420). .bss starts where d_actor.cpp's actor list ends (0x0209b468..0x0209b470). mwcc sorts a TU's .data and .bss objects by size as one list (notes/mwccarm-codegen.md 6dg). Both runs ascend: 1, 4 and 0x50 bytes in .data; 1, 4, 0x88 and 0x548 in .bss. The run ends with the 0x1000-byte heap data_0209baa0 (32-aligned, behind the 0x1c-byte gap data_0209ba84) and then a size drop at data_0209caa0. The heap is read only by func_020133bc, but it stays unclaimed here.

The 0x50-before-0x20 order at 0x0208e448/0x0208e498 is not a size-sort break and not a TU boundary. 0x0208e498 holds "/data/sound_data.sdat", which is 0x16 bytes, not 0x20. The next 8 bytes, 0x0208e4b0..0x0208e4b8, are _ZTV7dBase_c's preamble (0, then &_ZTI7dBase_c at 0x02086e78). func_020133bc passes the string to func_02050f34 as the archive path. Compiled as a literal, mwcc numbers it @1611 and emits it after every size-sorted named object, in its own .data section. That is retail's placement. It is left extern (data_0208e498) and outside the claim, because it ends at 0x0208e4ae, 2 bytes short of 0x0208e4b0. A claim ending at 0x0208e4b0 would need terminal linker fill, which tubuild licenses only for a claim that owns a whole module section. A deadstrip-data row cannot home the local @1611 either: compiler-only data policy runs before binding rewrites and skips locals.

Linkage. Objects with readers outside this TU (config/**/relocs.txt, overlays included) are globals: gSubSoundID, gMusicTrackModeOverride, gSoundMuted, gSoundInitialized, gMusicVolume, gSubVolume, gCurrentMusicID, data_0209b53c. Every other object is static in the source and is published STB_GLOBAL by a symbol_binding_rewrites row, because dsd cannot record a local symbol in symbols.txt. data_0209b484, data_0209b488, data_0209b48c, data_0209b4a4 and data_0209b4a8 keep their address names. The code shows how they are used (heap levels and two sequence handles), not what they were called.

Sound::Play and Sound::Play2D are defined void, matching the plurality of the tree. Callers that consume r0 (PlayCharVoice, PlayBank2_2D/PlayBank3_2D, func_02012174/func_0201277c/func_02012790) keep the extern "C" mangled spelling -- the same return-split the shard files already carried, banked in decl-agreement-baseline.json.
Sound::PlaySub and Sound::ChangeMusicVolume keep their literal mangled names: the `5Fix12IiE` encoding cannot be produced by any type this tree defines (the Fix12 wall, see include/Sound.h).

func_020133bc keeps its shard's opt_propagation-off pragma (load-bearing); the pragma is file-global under deferred codegen, so func_020132d8 and func_020133bc sit inside defer_codegen brackets -- func_020132d8 flushes the deferred queue under on and func_020133bc alone binds off. func_02012468 keeps the u64-mask launder that pins its register birth order.
Sound::Player::SetPlayableSeqCount (0x0204fadc), Sound::Func_02048e* (0x02048eb4..) and the rest of the sound-engine internals at 0x0204xxxx/0x0205xxxx are other TUs and are not claimed here.

Static initializer folded: data_0209b53c, the sound-object registry, is now defined in this TU as a SndRegTable (it was an extern char[], built by the handwritten src/unnamed/arm9/0207/__sinit_02074da8.c). SndRegTable gains an inline constructor that runs func_02011a5c, the registry's clear routine; mwcc emits __sinit_Sound.cpp and its .ctor word, both byte- and relocation-identical to retail with the object's .bss. The registry helpers still take char*, so their call sites pass (char *)&data_0209b53c. symbols.txt gains data_0209ba84 to anchor the claim's end: it labels the 0x1c-byte gap between the registry's end and data_0209baa0, the 32-byte-aligned 0x1000-byte sound heap func_020133bc hands to func_02049cd8; nothing references the gap.
